correctness.summary: ShouldStop aborts the search when timer > 100000000 and returns 0 without having explored the remaining subtree, leaving *best at whatever clique size was found before the cutoff. For an 'Exact' maximum-clique solver this can silently return a clique size smaller than the true maximum on large valid inputs, i.e. a wrong (non-maximum) result rather than the exact answer.
correctness.triggeringInput: Any graph large/dense enough that the Tomita-style recursion performs more than 1e8 node visits before completing (e.g. a near-complete graph on ~80+ vertices). On such an input Run returns *best truncated to the partial search result instead of the true maximum clique size.
correctness.rootCause: The timer guard is a hard step-count cutoff that returns 0 mid-search without signalling incompleteness, so callers cannot distinguish an exact answer from a truncated one; the reported *best may be below the true maximum.
correctness.suggestedFix: Either remove the step cutoff for the exact contract, or surface an 'incomplete/timed-out' flag (e.g. return a sentinel or out bool) so the caller knows the result is not proven optimal, rather than returning a silently non-maximum best.

perf.summary: The bound check `solSize + candSize <= *best` is duplicated: once in ShouldStop (called at entry) and again inside the while loop; and timer++ runs every node via a ref-passed counter.
perf.currentCost: ShouldStop is a non-inlined call at every Search entry doing timer++ plus the same bound the while-loop re-checks. The redundant bound costs an extra load of *best and compare per node.
perf.proposedChange: Mark ShouldStop with [MethodImpl(MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining)] (the using is already imported). Optionally fold the entry bound into the existing while-loop guard `if (solSize + candSize <= *best) return 0;` which already runs first iteration, removing the duplicate compare at entry.
perf.rationale: Inlining removes call overhead on the hottest path of an exponential search; eliminating the duplicate *best load/compare shortens the per-node critical path. AggressiveInlining on hot leaf methods is exactly the prescribed pattern.
perf.risk: The timer cutoff (timer > 100000000) must still fire; if folding the bound, keep timer++ and the timer check intact. Note: candSize==0 path returns before the while loop, so the entry bound is needed only when candSize>0 -- which the while guard covers. Verify the candSize==0 success path is still reached before any bound return (it is: the `if (candSize == 0)` check precedes the loop).

perf.summary: RemoveCandidate does an O(candSize) linear search for v, but v is always currentTmp[0] (the just-processed pivot), so removal is O(1).
perf.currentCost: After processing, v was read as currentTmp[0]. RemoveCandidate then scans the whole array to find v and swap-with-last, an O(candSize) pass per node, redundantly re-locating a known position 0.
perf.proposedChange: Since v == currentTmp[0] at the call site, replace RemoveCandidate's loop with `candSize--; currentTmp[0] = currentTmp[candSize];` (swap-remove index 0 with last). Pass the known index 0 instead of searching by value.
perf.rationale: Turns an O(k) removal into O(1), removing an entire linear pass per recursion node in an exponential algorithm -- a real asymptotic-per-node improvement of the maintenance cost.
perf.risk: Correctness hinges on v being exactly currentTmp[0] and unique. FilterNeighbors reads from currentTmp and writes to nextCand (cand), not modifying currentTmp, so currentTmp[0] is still v at removal time. Candidates are distinct vertex ids, so value v occurs once. Order of remaining candidates changes but the algorithm is order-insensitive (it just enumerates), so the visited set is identical. Safe.

perf.summary: Hoist the adjacency row base adj + v*n out of the loop.
perf.currentCost: adj[v*n + currentTmp[i]] recomputes v*n each iteration of the candidate-filter loop.
perf.proposedChange: `bool* row = adj + v * n;` before the loop, then `if (row[currentTmp[i]])`.
perf.rationale: Removes one multiply per inner iteration in a loop that runs for every recursion node; strengthens to a single base add + indexed load that Burst lowers cleanly.
perf.risk: None; adj is read-only and v is constant within the call.

perf.summary: The dp parameter is never read or written anywhere in the file -- it is pure dead weight threaded through every recursive call.
perf.currentCost: long* dp is passed to Run and forwarded through every Search recursion but never dereferenced; extra register/stack slot per recursive frame.
perf.proposedChange: Remove dp from Search's parameter list (and from Run if the public API can change). If Run's signature must stay stable for callers, at least stop forwarding it into Search.
perf.rationale: One fewer pointer argument per recursive call reduces prologue/spill cost in the hot exponential recursion and clarifies the contract. Confirmed unused by full-file read.
perf.risk: dp is in the public Run signature; dropping it there is a breaking change. Dropping from the private Search is safe and behavior-preserving.
